{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOUDROfM8AAAABVYhNcw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BlR_zzg-53AM", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BlR_z", "number": 51, "title": "Preserve the last provisional transcript when final decoding is empty", "body": "## Problem

The retained simulated-streaming pipeline produces two different transcript stages for each utterance:

- provisional text while speech is active;
- a fresh final decode after the utterance endpoint.

In real use, including browser-tab audio, an utterance can sometimes produce useful nonempty provisional text but an empty final decode.

The current UI appends only nonempty final text and then clears the provisional display. In that case, text that the user already saw recognized successfully disappears and is never preserved in the committed transcript.

## Expected outcome

If the final ReazonSpeech decode for an utterance is empty, but that same utterance previously produced a nonempty provisional transcript, preserve the **latest nonempty provisional transcript for that utterance** as the committed fallback result.

Normal nonempty final results must remain authoritative and must never be replaced by provisional text.

Conceptually:

```text
latest provisional = "recognized text"
final = "better final text"
→ commit "better final text"

latest provisional = "recognized text"
final = ""
→ commit "recognized text"

no nonempty provisional
final = ""
→ commit nothing
```

This fallback should belong to the reusable local ASR behavior rather than being a DOM-only workaround, so microphone and browser-tab sources behave consistently.

Completion criteria must be executable and verifiable by an AI agent.

## Scope

- Track the latest nonempty provisional text per active utterance ID in the appropriate ASR-core/pipeline layer.
- When the matching final decode is nonempty, emit/commit that final result unchanged.
- When the matching final decode is empty or whitespace-only and a nonempty provisional exists for that utterance, emit a committed final result using the latest nonempty provisional text.
- When both final and all provisional results are empty, preserve the current behavior and commit no text.
- Clear fallback state when the utterance completes, a new session starts, Stop drains, Cancel/release occurs, or an error resets the pipeline.
- Keep fallback state isolated by utterance/session so stale provisional text can never be committed for a later utterance.
- Preserve the existing provisional UI semantics: provisional text remains unstable while speaking and is cleared after the utterance is committed.
- Keep ReazonSpeech, Silero VAD, utterance timing, browser-tab capture, microphone capture, and model configuration unchanged.

Prefer the smallest coherent change. Do not add transcript merging, confidence scoring, LLM correction, or general hypothesis-selection logic.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

Automated deterministic tests verify:

- nonempty final text wins over a prior provisional transcript;
- empty/whitespace final text falls back to the latest nonempty provisional for the same utterance;
- multiple provisional updates use the latest nonempty value;
- an empty provisional update does not erase a previously usable fallback;
- no provisional plus empty final produces no committed text;
- fallback text cannot cross utterance IDs or recognition sessions;
- Stop, Cancel/release, repeat sessions, stale worker results, and errors clear or isolate fallback state correctly;
- the application appends the fallback as final/committed text and clears the provisional display;
- existing microphone and browser-tab source behavior remains unchanged;
- current relevant unit/browser tests pass.

## Required post-merge verification

None.

## Context

The current local ASR core intentionally re-decodes the complete utterance for final output rather than copying provisional text.

That is desirable when the final decode is useful, but it creates a data-loss UX when the final decode is empty despite a useful provisional result.

This Issue adds a narrow safety fallback only for that empty-final case. It does not change how ordinary provisional or final recognition is performed.

Related:

- #35 — hayamimi-style provisional/final utterance handling
- #47 — reusable local ASR core
- #49 — browser-tab audio input
